data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2015 Results (Volume III: Students’ Well-Being) synthesizes cross-country patterns for 15-year-old students’ life satisfaction, schoolwork-related anxiety, achievement motivation, expectations for further education, sense of belonging, bullying exposure, parental involvement, family wealth/inequalities, and students’ activities outside of school (including physical activity and Internet use). The volume is based on PISA 2015’s computer-based assessment (with limited paper-based delivery in some systems) and student/school questionnaires, covering science as the major domain and including contextual measures relevant to well-being. It reports prevalence rates (e.g., shares of students with low life satisfaction or frequent bullying) and associations between well-being indicators and factors such as teacher support, disciplinary climate, parental activities, and extreme Internet use. The report emphasizes that PISA cannot identify causal effects of policies on outcomes, and it focuses on statistically significant differences/changes.
